name: artifact_explore
description: Act on the open 3D model (heart, eye, brain, lungs, kidneys, stomach, animal cell, plant cell, DNA, or an imported model). action: separate ('expand', 'explode', 'take it apart', 'show me the parts': the parts glide apart, each named), assemble, cut_open, whole (undo the cut), xray, xray_off, isolate ('show me the frontal lobe', 'just the valves', 'show me this lobe': those parts glow and come forward, the rest fade to a faint outline), focus (that part solid, the rest see-through, nothing moves), unfocus ('show all', 'put it back': every part again), turn (degrees, default 30), reset. For isolate and focus give part as the user said it: one part, a list ('frontal and temporal lobes'), a group ('the chambers', 'the arteries', 'the left side'), or 'this' for the part they're pointing or looking at. If the result has options, ask which; if no part matched it lists the real ones. Pass template (heart, eye, brain, cell, plant_cell, dna) when they name a model that isn't open. Say in a few words what changed.

part.description: For isolate and focus: the part as the user said it ('left ventricle', 'the valves', 'frontal and temporal lobes'), or 'this' for what they point or look at.

degrees.description: For turn: how far, in degrees (positive turns it to the right). Default 30.

mode.description: For isolate: isolate (default) fades the rest to a faint outline; highlight keeps the rest see-through.

expand.description: For isolate and focus: bring the parts forward and a little bigger (default true for isolate, false for focus).

template.description: The model the user named, if it might not be the open one: heart, eye, brain, lungs, kidneys, stomach, cell, plant_cell or dna.

name: artifact_press
description: Press one of the open artifact's own buttons, to play its walkthrough or animation: 'trace the blood', 'show the blood flow' / 'hide it', 'pause the beat' (heart); 'follow the light' (eye); 'tour the lobes' (brain); 'follow a protein' (cell); 'follow the sunlight' (plant cell); 'explain it', 'spin it' / 'stop spinning' (DNA); 'hide labels' / 'show labels'. Say it as the user did; the result says which button it pressed and, for a walkthrough, its captions in order with how long each is on screen: explain the steps in that order, one short sentence each, as they play. If nothing matches, the result lists the buttons there are.

button.description: The button as the user said it, or its label or id.

template.description: The model the user named, if it might not be the open one: heart, eye, brain, lungs, kidneys, stomach, cell, plant_cell or dna.

name: artifact_describe
description: What's open right now and what it can do: the artifact's title, its named parts and part groups, its buttons, its walkthrough captions and notes, its state (apart, cut open, X-ray, which parts are shown on their own), and pointed_at and looked_at: the part the user is pointing at or looking at, with what it does. Call it before explaining the open model or answering a question about it, and for 'what's this?' (answer from pointed_at, else looked_at).
